solution:
The region is restricted to the first quadrant since \(x \ge 0\) and \(y \ge 0\).

Line \(3x + 2y = 18\): x-intercept \((6, 0)\), y-intercept \((0, 9)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 18\), true, so the region for \(3x + 2y \le 18\) is the side of the line containing the origin (boundary included).

Line \(2x + y = 10\): x-intercept \((5, 0)\), y-intercept \((0, 10)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 10\), true, so the region for \(2x + y \le 10\) is the origin side (boundary included).

The boundary lines \(3x + 2y = 18\) and \(2x + y = 10\) meet where \(x = 2\), \(y = 6\), i.e. \((2, 6)\).

The feasible region is the intersection of all four half-planes: a bounded quadrilateral with vertices \((0, 0)\), \((5, 0)\), \((2, 6)\) and \((0, 9)\).

solution:
First quadrant only (\(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\)).

Line \(2x + 3y = 6\): intercepts \((3, 0)\) and \((0, 2)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 6\), true — the region for \(2x + 3y \le 6\) is the origin side (boundary included).

Line \(x + y = 2\): intercepts \((2, 0)\) and \((0, 2)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \ge 2\), false — the region for \(x + y \ge 2\) is the side away from the origin (boundary included).

The lines \(2x + 3y = 6\) and \(x + y = 2\) meet at \((0, 2)\).

The feasible region is a bounded triangle with vertices \((2, 0)\), \((3, 0)\) and \((0, 2)\).

solution:
Line \(3x + 4y = 12\): intercepts \((4, 0)\) and \((0, 3)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \ge 12\), false — the region for \(3x + 4y \ge 12\) is the side away from the origin (boundary included).

Line \(4x + 7y = 28\): intercepts \((7, 0)\) and \((0, 4)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 28\), true — the region for \(4x + 7y \le 28\) is the origin side (boundary included).

\(y \ge 1\): region on and above the horizontal line \(y = 1\). \(x \ge 0\): region on and to the right of the Y-axis.

Corner points: \(3x + 4y = 12\) meets \(y = 1\) at \((8/3, 1)\); \(4x + 7y = 28\) meets \(y = 1\) at \((21/4, 1)\); the Y-axis meets \(3x + 4y = 12\) at \((0, 3)\) and \(4x + 7y = 28\) at \((0, 4)\).

The feasible region is a bounded quadrilateral with vertices \((0, 3)\), \((0, 4)\), \((21/4, 1)\) and \((8/3, 1)\).

First quadrant only (\(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\)).

Line \(x + 4y = 24\): intercepts \((24, 0)\) and \((0, 6)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 24\), true — origin side (boundary included).

Line \(3x + y = 21\): intercepts \((7, 0)\) and \((0, 21)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 21\), true — origin side (boundary included).

Line \(x + y = 9\): intercepts \((9, 0)\) and \((0, 9)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 9\), true — origin side (boundary included).

Corner points: \(x + y = 9\) meets \(x + 4y = 24\) at \((4, 5)\); \(x + y = 9\) meets \(3x + y = 21\) at \((6, 3)\); \(3x + y = 21\) meets the X-axis at \((7, 0)\); \(x + 4y = 24\) meets the Y-axis at \((0, 6)\).

The feasible region is a bounded pentagon with vertices \((0, 0)\), \((7, 0)\), \((6, 3)\), \((4, 5)\) and \((0, 6)\).

solution:
\(0 \le x \le 3\) gives the vertical strip between \(x = 0\) and \(x = 3\); \(0 \le y \le 3\) gives the horizontal strip between \(y = 0\) and \(y = 3\); together they bound the square \([0,3] \times [0,3]\).

Line \(x + y = 5\): intercepts \((5, 0)\) and \((0, 5)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 5\), true — the region for \(x + y \le 5\) is the origin side (boundary included). It cuts the square at \((3, 2)\) and \((2, 3)\).

Line \(2x + y = 4\): intercepts \((2, 0)\) and \((0, 4)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \ge 4\), false — the region for \(2x + y \ge 4\) is the side away from the origin (boundary included). It cuts the square at \((2, 0)\) and \((0.5, 3)\).

The feasible region is a bounded pentagon with vertices \((2, 0)\), \((3, 0)\), \((3, 2)\), \((2, 3)\) and \((0.5, 3)\).

First quadrant only (\(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\)).

Line \(x - 2y = 2\): intercepts \((2, 0)\) and \((0, -1)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 2\), true — the region for \(x - 2y \le 2\) is the origin side (boundary included).

Line \(x + y = 3\): intercepts \((3, 0)\) and \((0, 3)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \ge 3\), false — the region for \(x + y \ge 3\) is the side away from the origin (boundary included).

Line \(-2x + y = 4\): intercepts \((-2, 0)\) and \((0, 4)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 4\), true — the region for \(-2x + y \le 4\) is the origin side (boundary included).

Corner points: \(x + y = 3\) meets the Y-axis at \((0, 3)\); \(-2x + y = 4\) meets the Y-axis at \((0, 4)\); \(x + y = 3\) meets \(x - 2y = 2\) at \((8/3, 1/3)\).

The feasible region is unbounded, lying above \(x + y = 3\), on the origin side of both \(x - 2y = 2\) and \(-2x + y = 4\), within the first quadrant; its corner points are \((0, 3)\), \((0, 4)\) and \((8/3, 1/3)\).

solution:
Let the company make \(x\) units of A and \(y\) units of B, with \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).

Silver: each A needs 3 gm and each B needs 2 gm, with at most 6 gm available: \(3x + 2y \le 6\).
Gold: each A needs 1 gm and each B needs 2 gm, with at most 4 gm available: \(x + 2y \le 4\).

Line \(3x + 2y = 6\): intercepts \((2, 0)\) and \((0, 3)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 6\), true — origin side (boundary included).

Line \(x + 2y = 4\): intercepts \((4, 0)\) and \((0, 2)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 4\), true — origin side (boundary included).

The two lines meet at \((1, 3/2)\).

The feasible region is a bounded quadrilateral with vertices \((0, 0)\), \((2, 0)\), \((1, 3/2)\) and \((0, 2)\).

solution:
Let the dealer buy \(x\) tables and \(y\) chairs, with \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).

Investment: \(1500x + 750y \le 150000\), which simplifies to \(2x + y \le 200\).
Storage: \(x + y \le 60\).

Line \(2x + y = 200\): intercepts \((100, 0)\) and \((0, 200)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 200\), true — origin side (boundary included).

Line \(x + y = 60\): intercepts \((60, 0)\) and \((0, 60)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 60\), true — origin side (boundary included).

Within the first quadrant the storage line \(x + y = 60\) lies entirely inside \(2x + y \le 200\), so that constraint is non-binding here.

The feasible region is a bounded triangle with vertices \((0, 0)\), \((60, 0)\) and \((0, 60)\).

solution:
\(4x - 18 \ge 0 \Rightarrow x \ge \dfrac{18}{4} = 4.5\).

In the XY-plane the boundary is the vertical line \(x = 4.5\). Test \((5, 0)\): \(4(5) - 18 = 2 \ge 0\), true, so the required region is the half-plane on and to the right of the line \(x = 4.5\) (boundary included).

\(-11x - 55 \le 0 \Rightarrow -11x \le 55 \Rightarrow x \ge -5\) (dividing by \(-11\) reverses the inequality).

The boundary is the vertical line \(x = -5\). Test \((0, 0)\): \(-11(0) - 55 = -55 \le 0\), true, so the required region is the half-plane on and to the right of the line \(x = -5\) (boundary included).

\(5y - 12 \ge 0 \Rightarrow y \ge \dfrac{12}{5} = 2.4\).

The boundary is the horizontal line \(y = 2.4\). Test \((0, 3)\): \(5(3) - 12 = 3 \ge 0\), true, so the required region is the half-plane on and above the line \(y = 2.4\) (boundary included).

\(y \le -3.5\).

The boundary is the horizontal line \(y = -3.5\). Test \((0, 0)\): \(0 \le -3.5\), false, so the origin is not in the region. The required region is the half-plane on and below the line \(y = -3.5\) (boundary included).

\(x \ge 5y\), i.e. \(x - 5y \ge 0\). The boundary \(x = 5y\) (i.e. \(x - 5y = 0\)) passes through the origin with slope \(1/5\); it contains \((0, 0)\) and \((5, 1)\).

Since the line passes through the origin, test another point, say \((1, 0)\): \(1 - 5(0) = 1 \ge 0\), true. So the required region is the side of the line containing \((1, 0)\) — the half-plane below the line \(x = 5y\) (boundary included).

\(x + y \le 0\). The boundary \(x + y = 0\) passes through the origin with slope \(-1\); it contains \((0, 0)\) and \((1, -1)\).

Since the line passes through the origin, test another point: \((1, 1)\) gives \(2 \le 0\), false; \((-1, -1)\) gives \(-2 \le 0\), true. So the required region is the side containing \((-1, -1)\) — the half-plane below-left of the line \(x + y = 0\) (boundary included).

\(2y - 5x \ge 0\), i.e. \(y \ge \dfrac{5}{2}x\). The boundary \(2y - 5x = 0\) passes through the origin with slope \(5/2\); it contains \((0, 0)\) and \((2, 5)\).

Since the line passes through the origin, test another point, say \((0, 1)\): \(2(1) - 5(0) = 2 \ge 0\), true. So the required region is the side containing \((0, 1)\) — the half-plane above-left of the line \(2y = 5x\) (boundary included).

\(1x + 51 \le y\), i.e. \(y \ge x + 51\). The boundary \(y = x + 51\) has intercepts \((0, 51)\) and \((-51, 0)\).

Test \((0, 0)\): \(0 + 51 \le 0\), i.e. \(51 \le 0\), false, so the origin is not in the region. The required region is the half-plane on and above the line \(y = x + 51\) (boundary included).

Line \(2x + y = 2\): intercepts \((1, 0)\) and \((0, 2)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \ge 2\), false — the region for \(2x + y \ge 2\) is the side away from the origin (boundary included).

Line \(x - y = 1\): intercepts \((1, 0)\) and \((0, -1)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 1\), true — the region for \(x - y \le 1\) is the origin side (boundary included).

Both lines pass through \((1, 0)\).

The solution is the unbounded region common to the two half-planes, with corner point \((1, 0)\).

Line \(x + 2y = 4\): intercepts \((4, 0)\) and \((0, 2)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \ge 4\), false — the region for \(x + 2y \ge 4\) is the side away from the origin (boundary included).

Line \(2x - y = 6\): intercepts \((3, 0)\) and \((0, -6)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 6\), true — the region for \(2x - y \le 6\) is the origin side (boundary included).

The two lines meet at \((16/5, 2/5)\), i.e. \((3.2, 0.4)\).

The solution is the unbounded region common to both half-planes, with corner point \((3.2, 0.4)\).

Line \(3x + 4y = 12\): intercepts \((4, 0)\) and \((0, 3)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 12\), true — the region for \(3x + 4y \le 12\) is the origin side (boundary included).

Line \(x - 2y = 2\): intercepts \((2, 0)\) and \((0, -1)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \ge 2\), false — the region for \(x - 2y \ge 2\) is the side away from the origin (boundary included).

\(y \ge -1\): region on and above the horizontal line \(y = -1\).

Corner points: \(3x + 4y = 12\) meets \(x - 2y = 2\) at \((3.2, 0.6)\); \(x - 2y = 2\) meets \(y = -1\) at \((0, -1)\); \(3x + 4y = 12\) meets \(y = -1\) at \((16/3, -1)\).

The feasible region is a bounded triangle with vertices \((3.2, 0.6)\), \((0, -1)\) and \((16/3, -1)\).

First quadrant only (\(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\)).

Line \(2x + 3y = 12\): intercepts \((6, 0)\) and \((0, 4)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 12\), true — origin side (boundary included).

Line \(2x + y = 8\): intercepts \((4, 0)\) and \((0, 8)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 8\), true — origin side (boundary included).

The two lines meet at \((3, 2)\).

The feasible region is a bounded quadrilateral with vertices \((0, 0)\), \((4, 0)\), \((3, 2)\) and \((0, 4)\).

solution:
First quadrant only (\(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\)).

Line \(3x + 4y = 12\): intercepts \((4, 0)\) and \((0, 3)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \ge 12\), false — the region for \(3x + 4y \ge 12\) is the side away from the origin (boundary included).

Line \(4x + 7y = 28\): intercepts \((7, 0)\) and \((0, 4)\). At \((0,0)\): \(0 \le 28\), true — origin side (boundary included).

The two boundary lines meet at a point with negative \(x\), which lies outside the first quadrant.

The feasible region is a bounded quadrilateral with vertices \((4, 0)\), \((7, 0)\), \((0, 4)\) and \((0, 3)\) — the strip in the first quadrant lying above \(3x + 4y = 12\) and below \(4x + 7y = 28\).
